newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom rises after fall on single deal - traders.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom rises after fall on single deal - traders.

text.p: Gas monopoly Gazprom was the strongest gainer in early trade in Russian shares on Monday after falling sharply on a single deal, which did not signal a start of a fall, dealers said..
At 0930 GMT Gazprom was traded at $0.485 after it fell to $0.301 from $0.445 at Friday's close.
Traders said there was only one deal at $0.301 in Gazprom, while best bid and offer were quoted at $0.440 and $0.510 respectively.

"It was a single deal, which does not indicate a new trend," said Alexei Goncharov, chief analyst at Russian Brokerage House. "If there was any indication that the market was falling, no one would hold those bid and offer prices."

Oleg Tatkov, a trader from Renaissance Capital, said Gazprom was still attractive as current market prices were much lower than the preliminary price of $14-16 the company's American Depositary Shares to be launched soon.
One ADS is equivalent to 10 ordinary shares.
